item.title: Defiant DeChambeau 'grateful' for LIV, vague on future plans
item.description: Bryson DeChambeau expressed confidence that LIV Golf's distinctive team format would be successful in the future (Justin Casterline) Bryson DeChambeau said on Sunday he does not regret joining LIV Golf and offered no new details of his future plans in his first public comments since the divisive tour announced it is shutting down. DeChambeau was arguably the highest profile member of a swathe of golf stars who defected from the traditional PGA Tour to free-spending LIV in 2022, turning the golf world on its head. The two-time US Open winner had continued to staunchly defend the rebel tour even after its Saudi backers pulled the plug this year, expressing optimism for a now-aborted "LIV 2.0" relaunch plan even as others like Jon Rahm jumped ship. With LIV announcing on Thursday that it will shutter for good, DeChambeau issued a statement expressing gratitude for his experience with the rebel tour. "I'm not going to rewrite the last four years. I made a decision I believed in, and I'm grateful for what came with it: playing in front of fans new and old around the world who rarely got to see the best players at home," he said. "The record crowds in Adelaide and Johannesburg will stick with me for the rest of my life. "I believed this game could reach more people, in more places, in a new way. I still believe that. And I gave it everything I had to keep team golf alive." DeChambeau expressed confidence that LIV Golf's distinctive team-based format would be successful in the future. "I still believe in team golf. It may look different in the future, but I still believe it's essential to growing the game," he said. Several former LIV stars have announced they will play on the DP World (European) Tour next season -- a potential route to one day returning to the US PGA Tour. DeChambeau, whose personal commercial ventures include a hugely popular YouTube channel, did not reveal his future competitive plans, beyond a scheduled appearance at next month's Nedbank Golf Challenge in South Africa. But the famously outspoken and self-confident star vowed to act with "humility and respect" in the future as he ponders his next step. "Arnold Palmer said no player is bigger than the game, and I want to acknowledge that, along the way, I've said some things that didn't help," he said. "Whatever comes next, I'll approach it with humility and respect for the people who carried this game long before me." Beyond the Nedbank Golf Challenge event, "I'll go about whatever is next the right way," he added. amz/js

item.title: Man Utd rescue Villa draw with incredible fightback, Chelsea stunned
item.description: Manchester United defender Patrick Dorgu (2nd R) celebrates after scoring against Aston Villa (Darren Staples) Manchester United rescued an incredible 4-4 draw against Aston Villa as two stoppage-time goals gave Michael Carrick renewed hope of avoiding the sack, while Chelsea suffered a shock 1-0 loss at Sunderland on Sunday. United boss Carrick was seconds away from heading into the international break on the back of another devastating defeat that would surely have led to his dismissal. But Carrick's side struck twice in the six minutes of additional time through Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu to leave their manager's future still uncertain. United are in the relegation zone and have not won in their last eight Premier League matches, so it is far from sure that Carrick will survive the axe. He had earned a stay of execution when United's hierarchy allowed him to remain in charge despite last weekend's loss at Chelsea. United responded by ending a nine-match winless run in all competitions as they came from two goals down to beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday. But United, who have only three wins in 15 games this season, were back in turmoil when they fell 2-0 down against Villa in the first four minutes at Old Trafford. Alysson struck in the first minute with a shot that squirmed under United keeper Senne Lammens. Nicolas Jackson slotted in the second three minutes later after a weak save from Lammens pushed the ball into his path. Bruno Fernandes got one back with a 16th-minute penalty after Boubacar Kamara fouled Matheus Cunha before former Villa midfielder Youri Tielemans slammed in United's 44th-minute equaliser. Villa's John McGinn converted a 48th-minute penalty following Diogo Dalot's clumsy challenge on Alysson. Leon Goretzka poked in Villa's fourth from close-range after United's Leny Yoro headed against his own crossbar in the 53rd minute. Yet Zirkzee's stoppage-time finish gave United hope and Dorgu headed their dramatic equaliser in the final seconds after a weak punch from Villa keeper Zion Suzuki. Carrick wore a bewildered look on his face as he walked down the tunnel towards an uncertain future, with United next in action at Liverpool on November 22. "Making it hard for ourselves. The goals are coming from individual mistakes. We need to tighten up," Carrick said. "But I thought we were the better team. If we get one, then anything can happen. We never gave up and never stopped believing." Chelsea arrived at the Stadium of Light hoping to bolster their bid to qualify for the Champions League via a top-four finish. Instead, they departed red-faced after an embarrassing loss to third-bottom Sunderland, who celebrated a league victory for only the second time this season. item.title: Gauff outlasts Pegula to win group opener at WTA Finals
item.description: Coco Gauff defeated fellow American Jessica Pegula in their opening group stage match at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells (Katelyn Mulcahy) Coco Gauff outlasted fellow American Jessica Pegula to win a tension-packed group stage opener 6-4, 6-7 (5/7), 6-2 on Sunday in the WTA Finals at Indian Wells. Two-time major winner Gauff fell behind 5-1 in the second set but saved three set points in the 10th game and captured five games in a row to seize a 6-5 edge. Pegula denied a Gauff match point and held in the 12th game to force a tie-breaker, then jumped to a 5-2 lead and forced a third set with a forehand return winner. Gauff seized a 3-0 lead in the third set and dominated from there, holding in the final game to take the match after two hours and 39 minutes when Pegula swatted a backhand beyond the baseline. "I was having a lot of fun," Gauff said. "I took a little break. First match in like a month. To play a tournament like this with no preparation is something I've never done in my career. "I'm just really happy to get through today. It was a tough match. It was 2 1/2 hours and I feel like every point was -- I don't know if you guys were holding my breath but me too, so just happy to be through. "I'm really proud of myself for this one." Gauff, the 2023 US Open and 2025 French Open champion, and Pegula had split 10 prior career matches, Gauff winning the Cincinnati final and a Wimbledon quarter-final this year in their most recent prior meetings. In the other Group One opener, reigning Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova defeated Marta Kostyuk 6-2, 6-4. Noskova, a 21-year-old Czech, needed only 86 minutes to defeat Ukraine's Kostyuk. World number one and reigning champion Elena Rybakina withdrew from the WTA Finals on Saturday due to a viral illness with Kostyuk replacing her at the California hardcourt event. Noskova improved to 3-1 against Kostyuk, all matches coming this year as both made the WTA Finals for the first time. Noskova won in three sets at the US Open fourth round in their most recent prior meeting and in the Wimbledon semi-finals, while Kostyuk won on her way to the Madrid clay crown. This year's WTA Finals were scheduled to be held in Saudi Arabia but in July were moved to Indian Wells after US military strikes on Iran in February and the subsequent war in the region. js/amz

The Eagles are headed into their bye week, and head coach Nick Sirianni was asked if the Eagles will make significant changes to their coaching staff while the team tries to resurrect its season. item.title: Hornets Injury Update: Latest On Brandon Miller, Expected Timelines For Kon Knueppel, Dennis Schroder
item.description: Credits: Imagn Images The Charlotte Hornets released their latest injury report with some updates on Brandon Miller , Kon Knueppel , Dennis Schroder , and other players ahead of their upcoming matchup against the Cleveland Cavaliers . Kon Knueppel (left hamstring strain), Brandon Miller (right hip strain), Dennis Schroder (left hamstring strain), and Grant Williams (right hamstring) are all listed out for this fixture. Meanwhile, Moussa Diabate (right quadriceps tendinopathy) is listed as questionable. “Injury Updates: Hornets guard Dennis Schroder has been diagnosed with a left hamstring strain, will be listed as out vs. the Cavaliers on 11/9 and will be reevaluated in two weeks,” the Hornets’ official PR page wrote on X. “Hornets forward Kon Knueppel has been diagnosed with a left hamstring strain, will be listed as out vs. the Cavaliers on 11/9 and will be reevaluated in four weeks,” it further added . This is a significant setback for the Hornets as three of their primary starters (Knueppel, Miller, and Diabate) may not play against the Cavaliers (two confirmed out, one questionable). Meanwhile, veteran talent coming off the bench (like Schroder and Williams) will also be limited over the next two weeks. What was initially feared to be groin tightness for Brandon Miller turned out to be a hip strain that may also keep him out for a few games. The star forward has been growing into the role of franchise face alongside Kon Knueppel since the team traded LaMelo Ball this season. But without a reliable second scoring option like Knueppel on the floor, the entire defense has usually focused on Miller. He averaged 20.6 points, 5.0 rebounds, and 2.2 assists while shooting only 35.6% from the field and 26.0% from behind the three-point line. While his overall production may not have suffered as much, his efficiency certainly has. With Knueppel’s return, a lot of the defensive pressure will likely shift to him as well, which will help Miller thrive further when they’re fully healthy. Kon Knueppel returned to action against the Brooklyn Nets last week after missing the first eight games of the season. Unfortunately, he aggravated his injury once again minutes into his return without scoring a single point. Meanwhile, Dennis Schroder has been averaging 10.2 points, 4.9 assists, and 3.6 rebounds while shooting 36.4% from the field and 20.0% from behind the three-point line. The injuries have significantly derailed the Hornets’ start to the 2026-27 season as they struggle with a 3-7 record in their first 10 games. But not much was expected of a rebuilding team like the Hornets anyway. However, with the league having flattened the lottery odds, this losing record may not be as useful as it once was, especially for tanking the season. But the Hornets fans will certainly have to wait out a period of potential losses before they play meaningful basketball once again. It remains to be seen how the Hornets perform in this period of low expectations.

item.title: WTGL Has ‘Surreal’ Debut as Newest Women’s Sports League
item.description: WTGL, the indoor team women’s golf league modeled after the men’s TGL league co-founded by Tiger Woods, debuted Sunday with high energy, plenty of celebrities in attendance, and some minor hiccups along the way. Los Angeles Golf Club beat New York Golf Club 3–1 at the SoFi Center, the same 1,500-seat venue in Palm Beach Gardens, Fla., where all matches in TGL are played, too. Excitement was evident among the six LPGA players competing in the league’s inaugural match. “It feels really surreal,” L.A.’s Michelle Wie West, who came out of retirement to join WTGL, said on ESPN after the match. No. 1-ranked women’s golf Nelly Korda did not join WTGL for its first season, and earlier this year criticized the league for separating men’s and women’s golfers instead of adding women’s players to TGL. But those who have joined WTGL are pleased with what they’re seeing so far. “This format is so different,” Wie West in her post-match press conference said. “I think for two hours, LPGA fans can witness our players in a whole different light, and I think we’ll attract new [fans].” L.A.’s Alison Lee added, “Getting more TV time for us is amazing. The more we can put women’s golf on people’s screen, hopefully more people will consume it.” Gaby López rounded out L.A.’s roster for the match, while Rose Zhang, Linn Grant, and Lydia Ko competed for New York. WTGL has five teams of five players each, with three competing per team in each match, which consists of 15 holes. The season-long purse is $11 million. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Among the sell-out crowd Sunday were a number of notable team and league investors, as well as fellow TGL players. L.A. owners Alexis Ohanian and Serena Williams New York vice-governor Andy Cohen (son of New York owner Steve Cohen) Former U.S. men’s national soccer team star Jozy Altidore, who is investor in TGL/WTGL parent company TMRW Sports NYGC men’s members Rickie Fowler and Alex Fitzpatrick, and women’s teammate Yana Wilson, who was not competing LAGC members Sahith Theegala (men’s) and Kiara Romero (women’s) LPGA Commissioner Craig Kessler TMRW Sports CEO Mike McCarley ESPN vice president Rosalyn Durant Watch Party ESPN’s coverage of the inaugural WTGL match was scheduled to begin at 3 p.m. ET but the network didn’t pick it up until 3:15 as the Arkansas-Virginia men’s basketball game ran long. Zhang hit the first shot in league history just as ESPN switched over. Several TGL matches during that league’s first two seasons also experienced delays due to ESPN’s college basketball coverage running long. Sunday’s match lasted just over two hours, which is typical for the 15-hole format. Most WTGL matches will be in primetime on Mondays or Tuesdays. The league has media rights deals with ESPN and Ion. TGL matches averaged 498,000 viewers in its first season and dipped slightly to 488,000 viewers in its second. item.title: John Harbaugh Reacts After Giants Beat Eagles in Week 9
item.description: John Harbaugh Giants Getty New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh shared his reaction after the Giants beat the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 9. For the first time since 2013, the Giants won on the road in Philadelphia, doing so with a 19-11 win in Week 9. With the victory, the Giants improved to 5-2-1 on the season and remained in first place in the NFC East. John Harbaugh Reacts to Big Win Over Eagles in Week 9 Speaking to reporters after the Giants beat the Eagles in Week 9, Harbaugh shared his reaction to the team’s huge road win. “This is what the NFL is. It’s tough. It’s crazy town. It’s hard. Every team is really good. These guys were fighting for their lives. You could see it in the way they were playing, but we still overcame what we had to overcome, and we won the football game. It’s a big deal,” Harbaugh said. Despite starting QB J.J. McCarthy being banged up in the game , backup QB Jameis Winston came in off the bench and threw a clutch touchdown that helped the Giants win. Giants Battle Washington in Week 10 TNF Game The Giants now have a short week on deck, as they battle the Washington Commanders in Week 10 at home on Thursday Night Football. The last time the Giants and Commanders met earlier this season, the game ended in a rare tie, so this will be a key game for both teams as they both try to keep pace in the tight NFC East division race. But right now, the Giants seem to have the upper hand over the other teams in the division, as the Commanders and Eagles have struggled and the Dallas Cowboys have been very inconsistent. With Harbaugh as the Giants’ head coach, the team seems to have newfound confidence in themselves as they are trying to win their division for the first time since 2011, when they last won the Super Bowl. Despite the Giants suffering through many major injuries this season, including to quarterback Jaxson Dart, the team has managed to stay afloat as everyone is pulling their weight in all facets of the game. Star Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua injured his knee on the team’s final offensive snap on a 5-yard carry with just under two minutes to play, ESPN’s Adam Schefter and NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo . All-Pro WR Puka Nacua suffered a knee injury on the Rams’ final offensive snap today, and will undergo an MRI on Monday to determine the extent of the injury, per @MikeGarafolo and me. The team does not believe he suffered a torn ACL, but the imaging Monday will tell more. pic.twitter.com/S264w2Fe0A — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 8, 2026 After Nacua’s third-down carry didn’t pick up a first down and led to a Los Angeles punt, the Rams defense stopped a Commanders drive that reached deep into Los Angeles territory as time expired to earn the win. Prior to the injury, Nacua, the former BYU and Orem High star, was having another standout day. INSANE TOUCHDOWN CATCH FROM PUKA NACUA 🤯 📺 @NFLonFOX | #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/2cNavRnTCJ — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) November 8, 2026 That gave the Rams a 20-13 lead, and Los Angeles kept Washington from tying the game. item.title: Meriden-born NFL player John Jenkins of Baltimore Ravens visits North Haven police
item.description: Baltimore Ravens player John Jenkins from the NFL, a native of Meriden, visits with officers at the North Haven Police Department on Sunday. (Courtesy of the North Haven Police Department) NORTH HAVEN - What to do a when one of the NFL's longest-tenured defensive linemen pays your police department a visit? This was the position North Haven officers found themselves in Sunday when the Connecticut-born Baltimore Ravens defensive tackle John Jenkins came to call. "No big deal. Just another day at North Haven PD," the department posted Sunday afternoon along with photos. The 6-foot-3, 360-pound Jenkins, 37, was born and raised in Meriden. He starred as a defensive lineman for Maloney High School's Spartans, later earned a scholarship to play for the University Georgia and then entered the NFL as a third-round draft pick by the New Orleans Saints in 2013. Wearing Nike slippers and a hoodie, Jenkins struck a pose with officers who tried "to play it cool," North Haven police said. "Not everyone gets a visit like this. Just saying." The department on Sunday night said Jenkins grew up with one of North Haven's police officers, happened to be in the area and stopped by to say hello. Jenkins was able to be in Connecticut on a football Sunday because the Ravens already played Jacksonville on Thursday night in this week's schedule. item.title: The good, the bad, the s—t that gets you beat from Patriots vs. Packers
item.description: Ahead of his first training camp as Patriots head coach in 2025, Mike Vrabel explained that he was judging his team’s performances by three distinct categories: the good, the bad, and the s—t that gets you beat. If Vrabel looks at his team through those specific categorizations, we shall follow his lead. The New England Patriots were thoroughly dominated on Sunday by the Green Bay Packers. Despite both teams entering the game with identical 5-3 records, only one looked the part. The other, meanwhile, struggled from start to finish and ultimately suffered one of its worst losses in recent memory. With that said, let’s dive into our breakdown of the good — sort of — and the not-so-good from the 45-27 loss at Gillette Stadium . The good: Rare opportunities We typically try to be positive around these parts of the world wide web, but the glass is nowhere near to half full coming out of Sunday’s game. The search for anything good from the contest therefore has to yield some creative results. So, how about this: the Patriots were able to get some of their lesser-used player some increased playing time. Whether it was backup quarterback Tommy DeVito or multiple special teamers, they all got some rare in-game reps courtesy of the blowout defeat. Of course, given that New England suffered multiple injuries, they might need those backups to step up in the coming weeks. The bad: Star players One common theme for the Patriots on Sunday was their best players not holding up their end of the bargain: quarterback Drake Maye and cornerback Christian Gonzalez had rough days, to say the least. Maye seemingly reverted to his early-season self, tossing three more interceptions to contribute to Green Bay pulling away seemingly from the get-go. His first pass of the day already set the tone: an apparent miscommunication with wide receiver Mack Hollins, who returned from a four-game injury absence, led to an uncontested interception that was returned all the way to the New England 9-yard line. Two plays later, the Packers were up 7-0. That was the opening of the floodgates for the team and its quarterback. Maye finished 21-of-38 for 299 yards with three touchdowns and interceptions apiece. He finished with -0.13 expected points added per play. Gonzalez, meanwhile, played the worst game of his career. The highest-paid cornerback in football was in the area or in direct coverage on multiple big plays. While not all of the blame might fall directly on him — whether it was bracket coverage not working as intended, communication breakdowns, or defensive calls asking him to give some cushion underneath — the bottom line remains: he didn’t play up to his abilities. According to Erin Andrews of the Fox Broadcast team, his return to the game is questionable. Jacobs left the game early in the first quarter. It looked like Jacobs’ hand or finger got caught in the facemask of defender Craig Woodson on his last rushing attempt. His hand was bent backwards. Jacobs had four rushes for five yards in the Packers’ Week 9 game against the New England Patriots when he left with his hand injury. The team is currently leaning on Pierre Strong with Jacobs out. They also have MarShawn Lloyd as an option. Jacobs went to the locker room, but is currently back on the Packers sideline. There is a chance he will be returning to the game on their next drive. Green Bay Packers Lose RB Josh Jacobs to Hand Injury The Packers’ running game has been a disaster all season. It was expected to get better with the return of Jacobs. However, Jacobs has been slow to hit the ground running. He had 11 rushes for 36 yards in the team’s first game with him in the lineup after being on the Commissioner’s exempt list. The following week, he had 21 rushes for 39 yards. However, he has been an impactful player in the passing game. Jacobs had five catches for 55 yards in his first game back. He added six catches for 13 yards the next game. Green Bay is expected to lean pass-heavy without Jacobs. Both Matthew Golden and Christian Watson are having strong games. Jordan Love has over 130 yards in the first quarter, and the Packers lead 14-0 after one quarter. However, they will have to lean on someone to run the ball to close out the game. Packers Run Game Woes Continue Jacobs missed the first six weeks after being charged with misdemeanor criminal damage charges. Strong and Chris Brooks have split the passing-down-back role. Neither is expected to provide much on the ground. Lexi Thompson will play while six months pregnant in the Women’s TGL’s opening season, a move that forces major changes to her swing and equipment. item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers infielder Hyeseong Kim became a sports ambassador for his hometown of Goyang in South Korea. item.title: Former Michigan QB J.J. McCarthy Returns From Hip Scare
item.description: Former Michigan Wolverines quarterback J.J. McCarthy was making his second consecutive start for the New York Giants on Sunday, and it nearly ended early in Philadelphia. With 12:02 left in the third quarter and the Giants trailing 8-6 , McCarthy ran for three yards and Eagles linebacker Zack Baun caught him from behind. He left with a hip injury, and Jameis Winston came on in relief. The Giants listed McCarthy as questionable to return after he exited the game . He spent the drive in the locker room, tossing a football to keep warm while Winston worked, and he was back under center on New York’s next possession. Baun hurt his back on the same play and was ruled questionable himself. New York Giants quarterback JJ McCarthy, is shown during pregame practice, Sunday, October 4, 2026, in East Rutherford. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) J.J. McCarthy Credits the Giants Training Staff After New York’s 19-11 win, McCarthy handed the credit for the quick turnaround to the people who patched him up. “I can’t thank the training staff enough for helping me get back on the field as fast as possible,” he said . Giants coach John Harbaugh liked what the return said about his quarterback. “That’s big to fight through that kind of thing, fight through an injury, go back in, take care of it, get back out there,” Harbaugh said. McCarthy’s Day Before and After the Hip Injury McCarthy finished 12-of-19 for 127 yards with no touchdowns and no interceptions, and he ran four times for 22 yards. His longest carry, an 11-yarder, came after he returned. He was sacked five times. Winston went 6-of-8 for 71 yards in relief and threw the game’s lone touchdown, to Isaiah Likely, which put New York ahead 13-8 in the third quarter. Giants Host Washington on a Short Week New York hosts the Washington Commanders on Thursday, Nov. 12 at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video, a three-day turnaround. The Giants are 5-2-1 and lead the NFC East; Washington is 2-5-1. McCarthy said afterward that the hip was feeling good and that he would do his best to be ready for Thursday. A short week leaves a hip very little time to settle down, and if it holds him out, Winston would most likely get the start.
